As a Global Virtual Card Payment Administrator, you will serve as a specialist in our global Accounts Payable team located in Santa Clara, CA.
You will lead the strategy, administration, expansion, and control of our virtual card payment program across the Americas, EMEA, and APAC.
You will collaborate with card-issuing banks, suppliers, Treasury, regional AP teams, and internal partners.

section_responsibilities:
Support NVIDIA's worldwide virtual card payment initiative across all regions and legal entities, handling card payment cycles, card issuance, spending limits, and payment file exchanges between SAP and our card-issuing banks' systems.

Use AP spend analysis to identify card-eligible suppliers across regions.
Run targeted onboarding campaigns and grow program adoption and spend volume worldwide.
Address complicated supplier and bank customer inquiries involving virtual card payments, including declined, expired, or unprocessed cards, remittance difficulties, and payment rejections, spanning multiple time zones.

Support SOX adherence and audit readiness for the global virtual card program, including user access reviews, segregation of duties, payment approvals, and control evidence, while ensuring alignment with local regulatory requirements.
Mentor AP team members, establish global procedures, standards, and supplier-facing materials, and independently lead automation and process-improvement initiatives across the card payment process.

Experience with virtual card platforms from major global and regional issuers (e.g., Citi, HSBC, American Express) and their payment file and remittance processes.
Hands-on experience with Coupa Pay, including virtual card and invoice payment configuration, payment runs, supplier enablement, and reconciliation, with SAP integration experience a plus.
Understanding of SAP payment runs, vendor master data, bank integrations, and AP reconciliation.
Proven track record independently leading supplier enablement programs and cross-functional payment projects across multiple countries or regions with minimal direction.
Understanding of multi-currency and cross-border payments, payment controls, fraud prevention, and SOX requirements related to disbursements.
Awareness of country-specific requirements such as VAT and local payment regulations is also needed.
Advanced Excel and data analysis capabilities, with the ability to examine large spend datasets, develop arguments, and pinpoint program opportunities.
Practical experience applying AI tools and capabilities, including Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor, in a finance or business context.

Proficiency in one or more additional languages (e.g., Mandarin, Hebrew) to support suppliers and teams in key regions.

Most engineering careers start with tasks someone else defined, on problems someone else identified.
This one doesn't.
NVIDIA has reinvented computing more than once - the GPU, deep learning, the infrastructure that runs modern AI.
Today, as accelerated computing reshapes every industry from healthcare to robotics to scientific discovery, the silicon that powers it has never mattered more.
The Silicon Co-Design Group is where design intent becomes silicon reality, across consumer, professional, server, and automotive products.
As a new graduate here, you will be in the lab on real silicon from day one - owning work, not shadowing it - and when the silicon teaches you something the model didn't predict, your findings will shape the features that go into the next chip.
section_responsibilities:
Own characterization of pre-production silicon - speed, performance, power, yield, and quality - from early bring-up through production sign-off.
Define and refine features.
Evaluate new silicon capabilities against real-world use cases, quantify the benefit and cost of architected features post-silicon, and provide the data that determines what gets built into future products.
Build methodologies that last.
Develop characterization and validation methodologies that close the simulation-to-silicon gap, correlate measured behavior to design, and scale across products and generations.
Drive failure analysis.
Form hypotheses, design experiments, trace root causes across circuit, firmware, and software layers, and don't stop until the answer is confirmed.
Analyze real-world workloads - LLM inference and training, generative AI, AAA games, autonomous driving stacks - to push best-in-class performance and energy efficiency.
Build and deploy AI-driven analysis flows, intelligent data pipelines, and automated triage tools that expand coverage and compress cycle time.
Build tools the team runs on - automation for characterization, data collection, test execution, and analysis.
What you build will be used.
section_requirements:
BS, MS, or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or Systems Engineering.
Solid fundamentals in digital design, computer architecture, circuit analysis, signal integrity, and statistics - the kind you can apply under pressure, not just in coursework.
Proficiency in Python, C/C++, or equivalent.
You build things.
You don't wait for a tool to exist.
The instinct to own outcomes.
When something is wrong, you notice.
When you notice, you act.
You don't need to check every box.
We care more about how you think, how you learn, and what you've built than whether your background maps perfectly to this list.
If this role excites you, apply.
section_preferred:
You've built something with AI, LLMs, or agentic workflows that solved a real engineering problem.
You've developed a methodology or framework that someone else adopted - your work became the standard, not just the solution.
You've evaluated a feature, weighed benefit against cost, and produced a recommendation that influenced a real decision.
Lab experience with oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, BERTs, or similar.
The chips your team works on power the world's most advanced GPUs, workstations, datacenter AI infrastructure, and autonomous vehicles.
The engineers who built them started exactly where you are.
The difference is they chose to start here - where the ownership is real, the methodologies you build shape future programs, and the features you define ship to the world.
If that's where you want to begin, we want to hear from you.
Learn more about NVIDIA.

section_intro:
Today, we are tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing - an era in which our GPUs act as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that understand the world.
Doing what has never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world's best talent.
NVIDIA's Silicon Co-Design Group is the team that gets every GPU, SoC, and CPU silicon program from first power-on to high-volume production.
We are hiring an HSIO Validation Engineer to own characterization and qualification of high-speed I/Os - PCIe, NVLink, NVLink-C2C, UCIe, USB, UFS, and Ethernet - on brand-new silicon serving datacenter, AI, and client markets.
Your bench is where silicon meets the signal - where every link train, jitter sweep, eye diagram, and protocol corner gets exercised before the part ships.
You drive characterization and debug for IO interconnects across silicon, board, firmware, and driver - designing tests that anticipate rack-scale deployment so marginality surfaces at die-and-board scale, never in a rack.
Your decisions show up in link margin, BER, power per lane, and the go/no-go calls that gate samples and production.
section_responsibilities:
Own end-to-end characterization and validation of high-speed IO - PCIe, NVLink, NVLink-C2C, UCIe, USB, UFS, Ethernet - from silicon die through package and board, on NVIDIA GPUs, CPUs, and SoCs.
Develop and execute validation test plans for silicon and SoC-level HSIO features - bring-up, corner qualification, stress, productization, and structured DOE across PVT, board, cable/connector, thermal, and firmware variables - left-shifting silicon failures before deployment.
Drive power characterization and optimization across IO interconnects under workload-representative stimuli (MLPerf-class patterns at silicon/board level) - analyze trade-offs across V/F, lane config, and protocol state - and feed back into design, firmware, and binning.
Drive systematic root-cause analysis for complex HSIO bugs - isolating contributions across silicon, package, board, firmware, and driver, with platform/thermal/mechanical partners when system context matters.
Convert rack-observed failures into silicon/board reproducers so future spins fix the root cause upstream.
Assess manufacturing and yield implications of HSIO margin distributions - identify gaps in scaling from chip to product, and feed back into binning and design.
Develop and improve validation methodologies, automation frameworks, and margin-tracking infrastructure - increase efficiency and coverage as platform complexity grows.
section_requirements:
BS or MS in Electrical or Computer Engineering (or equivalent), with 6+ years in post-silicon HSIO validation, characterization, or a closely related discipline.
Deep understanding of high-speed serial link protocols (PCIe Gen5+, NVLink, NVLink-C2C, UCIe, CXL) and the underlying SERDES architecture - equalization, link training, electrical characterization - with strong signal integrity and jitter knowledge.
Strong SI and PI fundamentals - S-parameters, eye diagrams, channel margin, crosstalk, return loss, PDN noise, jitter decomposition - and validation experience across silicon and platform boundaries (CoWoS/interposer/substrate, board), translating rack-environment effects into silicon/board characterization.
Hands-on with lab instrumentation (DSOs, BERTs, VNAs, protocol/logic analyzers, TDR), DOE/shmoo/margin-trending, and Python-based test automation - with a track record of driving cross-functional debug across chip, package, board, firmware, driver, and system teams.
section_preferred:
Hands-on experience with PCIe Gen5/Gen6 or NVLink validation on production silicon - link training, equalization tuning, BER margining, or compliance debug.
Prior SERDES, mixed-signal, or analog circuit design experience - sufficient to independently form hypotheses, design Sim-to-Si correlation experiments, and propose silicon/system-side fixes during debug.
Track record of translating rack-environment conditions (thermal, connector reliability, neighbor noise) into silicon/board characterization - finding marginality at die-and-board scale before it appears in the field.
Comfortable using AI productivity tools (Claude, Copilot, or equivalent) to compress log triage, regression analysis, scripting, and reporting workflows. #LI-Hybrid NVIDIA pioneered accelerated computing.

section_intro:
Autonomous agents now do real work across NVIDIA, and every piece underneath them keeps changing: models, harnesses, tools, skills, and plugins.
Evaluation is how a team knows whether a change made an agent better or quietly made it worse.
We're looking for a principal engineer to set evaluation strategy at every layer, from individual skills and MCP servers to whole agents and products, and to design how agents use those results to improve themselves.
Agents can already rewrite the skills and plugins they run on, then test whether the change helped.
Making that loop trustworthy is the hard part.
What does it take for an agent to get better on its own, and prove the improvement is real?
We're building a system that answers that question for every agent at NVIDIA.
Come build it with us!
section_responsibilities:
Build evaluation that works the same across harnesses, with automated checks on every change that catch regressions before users do.
Mine production traces for failures, new usage patterns, missing skills and tools, cost and latency hot spots, and successful runs.
Turn them into eval cases and improvement signals.
Evaluate the eval datasets themselves: coverage of real usage, duplicate cases, and how closely they match production.
Build the self-improvement loop for evolving harnesses: agents propose changes to their own skills, plugins, and harness configuration, and sandboxed evals test each one.
Only measurable gains ship, with human sign-off and limits agents can't change.
Create realistic enterprise environments: sandboxed replicas of issue trackers, code repositories, chat, and internal APIs, filled with synthetic or anonymized data, where agents safely run long, end-to-end tasks.
Measure multi-agent swarms as a team: how agents split work, whether handoffs succeed, and whether permissions hold at every hop.
Record how long each task takes and how many tokens it uses.
Keep evals honest: calibrate model and agent judges against human labels.
Catch agents that cheat, such as working backward from expected answers or reaching data and tools they shouldn't access.
We work closely with product, platform, and hardware teams throughout NVIDIA, and we help shape open evaluation standards and benchmarks across the industry.

section_intro:
NVIDIA is seeking a senior systems software engineer to help engineering teams run demanding build, simulation, and validation workloads efficiently and reliably.
Our Workload Systems Engineering team connects customer workflows with the infrastructure that performs them.
We develop self-service mechanisms and clear diagnostics, investigate performance and reliability across system boundaries, and deliver measured infrastructure improvements with the teams that own the underlying components.
Your responsibilities include enabling application configuration, remote execution, workers, hosts, GPU and CPU resources, storage, data paths, and on-target systems.
The position requires direct system evaluation: diagnosing causes of slow or failing workloads, trying alternatives in representative scenarios, applying improvements with others, and verifying customer advantages.

Build shared self-service and validation mechanisms that let engineering teams configure and use supported infrastructure workflows with less manual assistance.
Give customers and on-call teams useful diagnostic views across application, submission, remote-execution, and host or target layers so they can identify where failures and slowdowns originate.
Set performance and reliability benchmarks for representative workloads.
Apply profiling, metrics, traces, and controlled experiments to pinpoint the changes that make a difference.
Evaluate and improve compute and GPU selection, scheduling and placement, concurrency, worker and runner configuration, resource sharing, caching, and input/output paths.
Make retry causes, recovery outcomes, and wasted execution capacity visible.
Work with component owners to eliminate recurring failures and unnecessary re-execution.
Implement and validate infrastructure-level changes with application, build and CI, remote-execution, and infrastructure teams.
Measure the effect on turnaround, successful efficiency, stability, usable capacity, and cost.
Turn successful investigations into supported workflows, diagnostics, documentation, and clear customer handoffs.
section_requirements:
Over 8 years of solid software engineering experience working with production compute infrastructure, distributed systems, large-scale build and test systems, or comparable systems software.
Hands-on experience debugging complex performance or reliability issues across software and hardware boundaries using logs, metrics, traces, profiling, and experiments.
Proficiency in a systems programming or automation language and experience delivering tested changes into production infrastructure.
In-depth experience with Linux and proficiency in one or more of these fields: GPU systems and drivers, scheduling and resource management, remote execution or CI infrastructure, storage and data paths, or host and container infrastructure.
Ability to work across teams with different component ownership, turn ambiguous symptoms into a clear technical plan, and explain results to engineering customers.
A degree in computer science, computer engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
section_preferred:
Experience with GPU sharing and isolation, CUDA execution behavior, MIG or MPS or equivalent experience, GPU driver diagnostics, or high-performance computing workloads.
Experience with workload placement, CPU and GPU concurrency, NUMA, cloud-instance benchmarking, or cost and performance tradeoffs.
Familiarity with Bazel, remote execution, build front ends, simulation or replay workloads, and hardware-in-the-loop validation.
Experience improving file-system, caching, networking, or high-throughput data paths under concurrent workloads.
A record of building customer self-service or observability tools and using incident and retry data to drive verified reliability improvements.

job_title: Senior Infrastructure Security Engineer – EDA Clusters
location: US, CA, Remote, United States of America
section_intro:
Securing NVIDIA's EDA clusters is not a matter of deploying a standard security stack.
The workloads are too large, too long-running, and too performance-sensitive for an off-the-shelf playbook to simply apply.
That constraint is the job.
You'll be an individual contributor on Infrastructure Security Engineering for EDA Clusters, the team that implements security controls across the compute, storage, and networking that NVIDIA's hardware engineers design silicon on - spanning on-prem data centers and multi-cloud.
You will sit alongside the engineers who run these clusters 24x7, close enough to deploy a control, investigate a behavior, and change the running environment yourself.
This is hands-on build work, not control review.
You'll decide where conventional tooling applies, where it actively cannot, and then engineer the alternative.
If your depth is in large-scale compute, networking, or storage infrastructure at a hyperscaler, a security product company, or anywhere fleets and fabrics are the day job, and you've carried real accountability for the security properties of those systems, you're who we want to talk to.
We don't expect fluency in every security product category.
We expect you to own outcomes and pick up the remaining domain breadth fast.
Security engineering here is engineering: code, instrumentation, and secure-by-default infrastructure - not tickets, exceptions, and spreadsheets.
section_responsibilities:
Build and operate security controls and telemetry for EDA compute, storage, and networking - design, ship to production, then own them.
Engineer around hard constraints.
Protect multi-day, high-value compute jobs without degrading them.
Where heavyweight in-node agents are not viable, build the workable answer instead.
Make the network and platform the control plane.
Protection can't depend solely on what runs inside the node.
Instrument for detection.
Collect and normalize security signals from the fleet into our SIEM, and build the detections and dashboards that turn it into something actionable.
Log collection alone is not monitoring.
Investigate and respond.
Chase down EDA-specific threats and exposure, and execute containment and remediation hands-on with infrastructure and service owners.
Automate enforcement and evidence.
Infrastructure-as-code and policy-as-code so secure configuration is the default state, with compliance evidence produced as an engineering output rather than a manual exercise.
Run the lifecycle of the security technologies you own: selection, rollout, operation, and eventual replacement.
Work across boundaries.
Partner directly with data center operations, IT storage and networking, network engineering, CSP teams, and NVIDIA's central security organization on shared outcomes.
Think like an adversary.
Threat modeling and mitigation planning across network, storage, and compute.
section_requirements:
8+ years of hands-on infrastructure or infrastructure-security engineering across on-prem and cloud environments.
Strong Linux depth - you are comfortable at the system level, not just the console level.
Real experience operating or securing compute fleets at scale: provisioning, lifecycle, and the operational realities of long-running jobs.
Working networking expertise applied to large compute environments.
Programming/scripting fluency (Python, Go, or shell) used for automation, detection, and tooling you've shipped and maintained.
Solid foundations in access control, authentication, segmentation, encryption, and vulnerability lifecycle.
A track record of landing changes with partners who don't report to you.
Clear written and verbal communication - credible with individual engineers and with leadership.
A Bachelor's degree in a relevant engineering field or equivalent experience.
section_preferred:
Security or platform engineering inside EDA, HPC, or large research-cluster environments.
Breadth across security domains - IAM, EDR/XDR, CNAPP, CSPM, zero-trust architectures - or a demonstrated pattern of picking up new domains fast.
Built or operated infrastructure security capabilities at a hyperscaler or a security product company - you engineered detection and enforcement systems rather than deploying someone else's.
Experience with kernel- and fabric-level observability and enforcement - eBPF, in-line and out-of-band inspection, DPU/SmartNIC offload - as an alternative to heavyweight in-node agents.
Contributions to open-source security or infrastructure tooling.
We have some of the most forward-thinking and talented people in the world working for us and, due to outstanding growth, our world-class engineering teams are growing fast.
If you're a creative and autonomous engineer with real passion for technology, we want to hear from you.

location: Taiwan, Hsinchu, Taiwan
section_intro:
By submitting your resume, you're expressing interest in our 2027 RDSS (Research and Development Substitute Services) program.
Please confirm your eligibility with the local district office before applying for the role.
Welcome to the world of NVIDIA, where innovation knows no bounds.
We've been at the forefront of technology for over two decades, and our groundbreaking invention of the GPU in 1999 revolutionized not only an industry but also the very way we engage with computers, robots, and autonomous vehicles.
Today, NVIDIA stands at the forefront of AI computing and is committed to continue pushing the limits of what is achievable.
Join us on this remarkable journey as we shape the future every day.
Today, visual computing is becoming increasingly central to how people interact with technology, and there has never been a more exciting time to join our team!
We are looking for a skilled, creative, and highly motivated RDSS Intern in the field of Electrical Failure Analysis to join the electro-optical FA team in Hsinchu, TW.
section_responsibilities:
Your main job will be to perform electro-optical failure analysis including Photon-Emission, Laser-Voltage-Probing and Soft-Defect-Localization (aka SDL, LADA...) to support product development, design-debug, yield-ramp, reliability and customer return analysis of advanced flip chip devices manufactured in the most advanced CMOS technology.
The work requires in-depth understanding of scan-chain based logical test.
Based on production test results (e.g. error-logs, flop mapping and SW-diagnosis) you will narrow down the logically failing area with the goal of locating the one failing FET or cell out of the whole chip.
Most analyses will require you to setup test-loops within our Advantest 93k tester SW.
Additionally, you will use CAD layout tools for in-chip navigation and circuit simulation tools to aid your analysis.
The goal is that our EFA results enable different Physical FA teams local and abroad to find the actual physical root-cause.
Based on our work and the resulting PFA findings, our Foundry partners can improve their process technology and increase our product yield and reliability.
You will need basic Unix skills because the CAD, circuit simulation tools and 93k tester SW are all run in a Unix environment.
Design-debug and more complicated defect localizations will often require you working in multi-functional teams (e.g. with Design for Test, Test-Engineers and Product-Engineers, sometimes around the globe..) including presenting & explaining your results.
To guide such team and PFA efforts you will need deep understanding of transistor physics, the CMOS fabrication processes and PFA tools/techniques such as SEM, TEM, FIB & AFM.
Support Die Probe Package second-source development for A16 FA readiness.
section_requirements:
Master's or PhD degree in Electrical/Computer Engineering or other related field Basic understanding of DFT for large-scale logical test (scan-chain based structural and at-speed testing and basics of test compression).
Experience working in a lab, setting up and debugging test environments. / Functional knowledge of transistor device physics & advanced CMOS manufacturing processes. / Test bring-up in the Advantest 93k test environment.
Knowledge of CAD layout tools, logic circuit simulation tools and Unix operating system. / Software languages that may be of use include PERL, TCL, C++, STYLE.
Good written and verbal communication skills are critical.
Learn more about NVIDIA.

Shape the Future of Validation.
Design and build the systems that turn cluster validation from a manual exercise into repeatable, verifiable software.

Core Development.
Design and implement cluster readiness and certification tooling in Go and Python that runs on Kubernetes and Slurm, including controllers, operators, CLIs, and scheduler integrations.
Benchmarking & Workloads.
Build a catalog of benchmarks and real workloads spanning communication (NCCL), compute, storage, diagnostics, training, inference, reliability, and security, with per-architecture expectations and clear pass/fail criteria.
Data Provenance.
Develop provenance and evidence pipelines that capture what actually ran, where it ran, and under which configuration, and that produce signed, auditable results.
Platform Integration.

Cross-functional Collaboration.Collaborate with internal platform, networking, and solutions teams and with cloud partners to root-cause performance and correctness gaps found by the tooling, and feed fixes back into platforms and reference architectures.
Open Source Contribution.
Contribute to the open-source Cluster Readiness Engine and related projects, including design documents, documentation, and reviews.
Technical Authorship.
Author design documents, runbooks, and operational guides that codify how clusters are validated and how results are interpreted.

section_intro:
Today, we are building software, systems, and research platforms that help scientists and engineers solve problems that were once out of reach.
We are looking for an Applied Research Scientist to join our computational engineering applied research team!

You will explore solver algorithms, build research prototypes, compare approaches on representative workloads, and help move promising ideas into software used by researchers, engineers, and partners.
The goal is not simply to port established CPU algorithms, but to rethink methods around massive parallelism, hierarchical memory, reduced synchronization, mixed precision, tensor-core computation, and multi-GPU systems.
This role connects numerical analysis, accelerated computing, production-minded software engineering, and the co-design of future AI-native engineering methods.
We are interested in candidates who enjoy working across math, code, hardware, and real engineering applications.
Come help us shape the future of simulation on GPUs!

Develop linear and nonlinear solver approaches, including Newton-Krylov methods, multigrid and AMG, domain decomposition, matrix-free algorithms, mixed precision methods, sparse iterative and direct methods, and preconditioning strategies.
Investigate when established CPU-oriented numerical methods should be reformulated or replaced for GPU architectures, including new approaches to synchronization-avoiding Krylov methods, GPU-native multigrid and domain decomposition, matrix-free implicit methods, mixed-precision algorithms, and sparse direct/iterative hybrids.
Evaluate algorithms on workloads in mechanics, contact, thermal-fluid systems, electromagnetics, semiconductor process and device simulation, EDA, multiphysics, and related CAE domains.
Collaborate with CUDA-X, Warp, solver engineering, NVIDIA Research, universities, and industry partners to move useful research from prototype to NVIDIA software capabilities.
Help shape the long-term applied research roadmap for GPU-native numerical methods and their evolution toward AI-native computational engineering.

Research or engineering experience with PDE discretization, finite element, finite volume, discontinuous Galerkin methods, nonlinear solvers, sparse linear algebra, preconditioning, or high-performance computing.

Serving as an AI Engineer on our AI Safety Engineering team, you will have a key and adaptable role in scaling methods to secure and align advanced AI systems.
Your early work will center on architecting and developing the fundamental elements of our safety infrastructure, emphasizing autonomous automation cycles.
To operationalize these automated workflows, you will partner with Research and Model Development teams thereby delivering novel models for harm detection, content moderation, dynamic guardrails, post-training, and groundbreaking automated research pipelines that push the limits.
This role is built for a tenacious builder and an inquisitive problem solver.
We want an engineer who thrives in ambiguity.
They must have the grit to overcome complex technical challenges and transform innovative safety concepts from raw ideas to scalable implementations.
section_responsibilities:
Architect Agentic Automation: Compose, build, and deploy foundational agentic automation loops that streamline workflows spanning safety evaluations, red-teaming, model testing, model post-training and ablations.
Develop Safety Models: Move from infrastructure automation towards training and implementing specialized systems for identifying harmful content, coordinating content quality, and run-time guard-railing.
Pioneer Auto-Research: Build and guide automated research frameworks.
These frameworks use LLMs and autonomous agents to discover new vulnerabilities.
They also generate or augment safety datasets for benchmarking or training and propose novel alignment techniques.
Scale Innovations: Take proof-of-concept safety interventions and research ideas and engineer them into robust, highly scalable solutions that integrate seamlessly into our production pipelines.
Cross-Functional Execution: Partner closely with researchers, platform engineers, and data scientists to bridge the gap between theoretical AI safety research and practical, technically focused automated systems.

Education: Bachelor's degree or Master's degree with equivalent experience in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Software Engineering, or a related field.
Experience: Candidates should have a strong track record in ML engineering or software engineering with 8+ years of experience.
Agentic Systems & Automation: Proven experience building complex, automated workflows using LLMs, including multi-turn tool-calling, orchestration, and autonomous agent loops.
Strong engineering fundamentals include deep proficiency in one or more languages such as Rust or Python.
Experience with machine learning frameworks like PyTorch is also required.
The focus is on writing scalable, maintainable, and highly optimized code.
Inquisitive Problem-Solving & Tenacity: A demonstrated ability to tackle open-ended, ambiguous problems.
You must be willing to experiment, fail, iterate, and relentlessly pursue solutions.
End-to-End Execution: The ability to own a project from the initial white-boarding of a research idea to the final deployment of a scalable production system.

Guardrails & Moderation: Hands-on experience developing, fine-tuning, or deploying models specifically built for harm detection, content safety (violence, hate, harassment, CBRNE, etc.) filtering, or run-time AI guardrails.
Auto-Research Experience: Contributions to projects that use LLMs to automate coding, data synthesis, or scientific research tasks.
Community & Collaboration: Active contributions to publicly available agent frameworks (e.g., LangChain, AutoGPT, Semantic Kernel) or AI safety benchmarking tools.

Reproducible Evaluation: Build reusable Python pipelines with versioned datasets, model configurations, and experiment tracking to reproduce results and compare performance across model releases.
Automated Red-Teaming: Develop tools to discover failure modes and expand evaluation coverage, incorporating human review to validate automated scoring and provide additional judgment.
Failure Analysis: Investigate model failures with researchers, document actionable findings, and develop regression tests to assess whether model changes resolve identified issues.
Results and Communication: Partner with platform engineers to store and aggregate evaluation results, and clearly communicate findings, limitations, and emerging risks to researchers and decision-makers.

We run Slurm and Kubernetes at large scale.
Our scheduling is coordinated and topology-sensitive on rack-scale systems.
We manage fair sharing and quotas for hundreds of research teams.

Elastic jobs recover from failure without losing progress.

Run Slurm as a cloud-native service on Kubernetes, and extend Kubernetes batch scheduling (Kueue and its ecosystem) for training, reinforcement learning, sandboxes and inference.
Build services around the scheduler: reservation automation, node-health-aware placement, workflow orchestration across clusters, and APIs that let other platforms submit and track work.
